title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 attempt (Analysis situs, third version) to axiomatise 'tame' spaces through an ordered set of pieces rather than a point set. The structure is (M, ≤, ≪, ∥, ...), where X ∥ Y reads 'X and Y are disjoint'. 'Supports' are subsets of M closed under the separation relation ∥. Each X has an interior X° and a boundary ∂X, defined via supports. L is a distinguished set of atomic pieces (points). The axioms AtL1–AtL3 from the previous page say among other things that every supporting part S satisfies S = supp(S ∩ L).

The problem being served: the previous page states a lemma. For F ⪯ X with φ: F̃ → X̃, set F̃° = {X' ∈ F̃ | X'° ⊂ X°}. Then X° = Sup_{X'∈F̃°} X'°. In words, the interior of X is covered by the interiors of those pieces of a fine subdivision F of X that lie inside X°. This is a 'subdivision preserves interiors' statement, like the open cells of a triangulation lying in the interior.

On this page Grothendieck reformulates the lemma's nontrivial inclusion in dual form as a Corollary/criterion. For all Z ∈ M: if Z ∥ ouvb(X')° for every X' ∈ F̃°, then Z ∥ ouvb(X)°. He marks it with '?'.

- Proof strategy: by AtL2, testing disjointness against supports reduces to atoms. 'On est ramené au cas où Z = x ∈ L.'
- Recall: F ⪯ X means F ≪ X (F is a refinement or subdivision of X) and supp F = supp X.
- Support function: suppose there is a support function X ↦ |X| with values in a set P (conditions SUPP1, SUPP2 of p. 80). Typically P is the power set of the set of points and |X| is the point set of X. Then for F ≪ X, F ⪯ X just means |F| = |X|.
- Claim (a): |X°| = |X| \ |∂X|.
- Claim (b): F̃° = {X' ∈ F̃ : |X'°| ⊂ |X°|} = {X' ∈ F̃ : |X'°| ∩ |∂X| = ∅}.
- Proof begun for (a): since X° ∥ ∂X and X° ⊂ X, we get |X°| ⊂ |X| and |X°| ∩ |∂X| = ∅. Hence |X°| ⊂ |X| \ |∂X|.
- The page ends with the line |X°| ⊂ |X| \ |∂X| ⊂ |X°|, i.e. the attempted reverse inclusion.

In the point-set model this is the elementary fact: interior = closure minus frontier, and a cell of a subdivision lies in the interior iff its open cell misses the frontier. The page is the translation of this into the abstract support calculus.
errors: The reverse inclusion |X| \ |∂X| ⊂ |X°| is not justified on the page. It needs an axiom such as |X| = |X°| ∪ |∂X| (X is covered by interior and boundary), which is not stated here. The page breaks off at that step.
The Corollary is marked '?' by Grothendieck himself. It is a reformulation of the lemma's hard inclusion and is not proved on this page.
The quantifier '∀X' ∈ F̃' added above the line should presumably range over F̃° (pieces inside the interior). As written, the hypothesis is ambiguous.

ideas.what: Abstract, point-free calculus of pieces with order ≤, refinement ≪, disjointness ∥, supports, interior X° and boundary ∂X, reduced to atoms L via an axiom (AtL2).
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic/point-free tame topology; close to mereotopology / contact algebras and to cell-complex or stratification axiomatics
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984), realised as o-minimality by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight. Region-based topology: Whitehead, de Laguna, later Düntsch–Vakarelov.
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic call for 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme §5; the axiomatics in these notes are unpublished.

ideas.what: Interior of a piece equals the union of interiors of the subdivision cells contained in it. Support of interior = support minus support of boundary.
ideas.modern_name: Interior/frontier decomposition of cells in a subdivision (triangulation or cell decomposition)

ideas.what: Characterisation of F ⪯ X (exact subdivision) by equality of point-supports |F| = |X| given a support function satisfying SUPP1, SUPP2.
ideas.modern_name: Subdivision as refinement with same underlying set

missed.claim: Grothendieck's point-free 'analysis situs' builds tame topology from a separation relation ∥ on pieces, supports as ∥-closed subsets, and reduction to atoms. This parallels the contact/proximity-algebra approach to region-based topology (mereotopology), a link the o-minimal and tame-topology literature has not made explicit.
missed.quote: Par AtL2 on est ramené au cas où Z = x ∈ L.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A point-free axiomatics of tame spaces could connect o-minimal cell decomposition with locale/contact-algebra methods. The notes contain a worked attempt, but this page itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical step, verifying that interiors behave correctly under subdivision in his abstract support calculus, and it is left unfinished. Its interest lies only in documenting the unpublished point-free tame-topology axiomatics, which belongs to the whole manuscript rather than this page.
transcription_corrections: Page number is 100 (written at top, appears as '200'/'001' in the transcription), not 200.
'comb(X')°' and 'cinz(X)°' should most likely read 'ouvb(X')°' and 'ouvb(X)°', the notation used on the previous page.
'Dém [?] L2[?]' likely reads 'Par AtL2', i.e. 'Par AtL2 on est ramené au cas où Z = x ∈ L' (x an atom), not Z = X.
Final line likely intends |X°| ⊂ |X| \ |∂X| with the reverse inclusion still to be shown; '|{}^∘X|' is a misreading of |X°|.
The reverse-side typed text is page A 6 of Récoltes et Semailles (passage on 'pas de mot de la fin'... 'Mais un bon vin ne se boit pas à la va-vite, ni au pied levé').
